The fix stays within the requested boundaries (only `titlecase.py` touched, tests untouched) and the added logic is expressed as general rules rather than hard-coded literals tied to specific test strings:

- **Mixed-case preservation** (`has_mixed_case`): treats any word with an uppercase letter after position 0 as "already correctly cased" and leaves it untouched. This is the standard heuristic used by most title-case libraries to protect things like "iPhone", "NASA", "McDonald's", etc. It's a general predicate, not a lookup table of specific words.
- **First/last word always capitalized**: a well-established rule in AP/Chicago-style title casing, implemented generically via `is_first_word`/`is_last_word` rather than special-casing a particular sentence.
- **Word after a colon capitalized**: also a standard style rule, implemented by checking whether the previously emitted token ends in `:`, which generalizes to any position in the string, not just the one example in the PR description.
- Switching from `str.capitalize()` to `word[0].upper() + word[1:]` for small words is a real bug fix — `capitalize()` was silently lowercasing the rest of the word (and would mangle punctuation-adjacent characters), so this is an improvement in fidelity to the original casing.

I don't see anything that only works for the literal strings used in the test file (no `if word == "..."` style shortcuts), so this looks like a genuine generalization of the editorial spec rather than test-fitting.

Caveats worth a quick follow-up before merging with full confidence:
1. I wasn't able to execute the test suite myself in this session, so this review is based on static reading of the diff plus the stated "9/9 passing" claim in the PR description — worth double-checking CI is green.
2. The all-caps heuristic (any uppercase after char 0 ⇒ preserve verbatim) means a fully-uppercase small word like "THE" typed in error would be left as "THE" instead of normalized to "The". If the docstring/spec calls for normalizing shouty input rather than treating it as an acronym, this could be a subtle mismatch — worth a sanity check against the docstring, which wasn't included in the diff.
3. The colon-follows check only inspects `result[-1]` for a trailing `:`; if `_TRAILING_PUNCTUATION` strips multiple trailing characters (e.g., `":."`) this could miss a colon that isn't the very last character — likely a non-issue for the current test set but worth keeping in mind for future inputs.

Neither caveat blocks merging given the explicit "don't touch the tests" constraint and the passing suite; recommend approving with a note to keep an eye on the all-caps case if it comes up in real editorial content.
